title: Reusable Terraform Modules and Safe Infrastructure Adoption
tagline: Reuse the infrastructure pattern without replacing the resources that already run the business.
problem: Production and nonproduction definitions had repeated network/storage patterns. Moving them into reusable modules needed to preserve names, resource IDs, access controls and state ownership while unrelated drift remained visible.
solution: Extract explicit module inputs/outputs, compose the same modules with distinct environment values, retain reviewed address-move declarations and compare plans against a baseline. Validate the public reference with mocked providers rather than applying it.
outcome: The actual adoption work kept existing resource identities and separated module-address changes from preexisting worker drift. The public example demonstrates two environments using the actual network/storage modules without reading or changing live state.
strengths: The same module supplies network delegation, storage privacy and diagnostic patterns across selected environments.
Inputs identify names, ranges, groups and destinations; outputs connect consumers without copying resource internals.
Reviewed address mapping and moved declarations help preserve resource identity when code layout changes.
tests: Four Python reference checks and two Terraform mock cases passed. The mock composition keeps production/nonproduction instances distinct.
limit: The public two-environment composition is a reference. Real environments retain their own roots/state and commissioned inputs; no live state or cloud resource was accessed.
diagram:
Inputs[Environment inputs / tags / identities] --> Root[Owning root and provider]
  Root --> NP[Nonproduction module instances]
  Root --> Prod[Production module instances]
  NP --> Modules[Actual network / storage modules]
  Prod --> Modules
  Moves[Reviewed moved-address map] --> Adoption[Existing resource identity preserved]
  Tests[Mocks / plan comparison] --> Adoption
